models.h2: Every American Standard furnace, and what we do for each one
models.intro: Find your series on the plate inside the lower door. Each one fails in its own ways, so each gets its own kind of visit.

series.name: Platinum
series.summary: Modulating gas valve, variable-speed blower, AccuLink communicating controls.
weDo: Diagnose communicating-control faults with the AccuLink thermostat linked in
Repair variable-speed blower motors and their control modules
Set up the modulating gas valve so it runs low and quiet, not on-off

series.name: Gold
series.summary: Two-stage burners and variable-speed blowers, built for quieter, steadier heat.
weDo: Replace inducer motors and pressure switches, then test the vent and hose
Check both gas-valve stages and set the high and low fire
Test the control board before replacing it, so you never pay for a guess

series.name: Silver
series.summary: The workhorse in Chicago bungalows and two-flats. Simple, and quick to fix.
weDo: Replace hot-surface ignitors and flame sensors on the same visit
Fix overheating and limit-switch shutdowns at the cause, not with a reset
Clean burners and blower wheel so it lights first time all winter

series.name: Older models
series.summary: Model plates we still open every winter, some 20 years and older.
weDo: Source discontinued parts, or a genuine equivalent that fits
Inspect the heat exchanger and test for carbon monoxide on every visit
Give you repair and replace numbers side by side, then let you decide

models.buildsNote: The number is in the model name on the plate

builds.name: Standard efficiency
builds.weDo: Vents up a metal flue into the chimney. We check the draft, the flue liner and the chimney connection along with the burners.

builds.name: High-efficiency condensing
builds.weDo: White PVC pipes out the side wall and a condensate drain. We clear snow-blocked vents, frozen drains and the trap every winter.

builds.label: AccuLink
builds.name: Communicating systems
builds.weDo: Furnace, thermostat and AC talk to each other. We read the fault history from the thermostat before we open a panel.

recentJobs.h2: American Standard furnaces we fixed this winter
recentJobs.intro: What the owner noticed, what we found and what it cost. Real jobs from our own invoices.

jobs.title: Lit, then shut off every few seconds
jobs.found: A coated flame sensor. Eight flashes on the board.
jobs.weDid: Cleaned the sensor, checked the flame signal on our meter, cleaned the burners.

jobs.title: No heat, no glow, locked out
jobs.found: A cracked hot-surface ignitor. Two flashes on the board after three tries.
jobs.weDid: Fitted a genuine ignitor from the van and checked the gas valve feeding it.

jobs.title: Hummed, then stopped before lighting
jobs.found: Snow over the PVC intake and a failing inducer motor. Three flashes.
jobs.weDid: Cleared the vent, replaced the inducer under warranty, filed the claim.

items.question: Will your repair affect my American Standard warranty?
items.answer: No. American Standard covers the parts. We fit genuine parts, check your registration by serial number and file the claim, so a covered part costs you labor only.

items.question: Where do I find my American Standard model number?
items.answer: On the rating plate inside the lower door, near the blower. Read us the model and serial number when you call and we'll bring the right parts.

items.question: Why is my American Standard furnace blinking red?
items.answer: The light is a fault code. Tell us how many times it flashes when you call, and our technician brings the parts for that fault.

items.question: Is it worth repairing a 15-year-old furnace?
items.answer: Often yes for an ignitor, sensor or switch. We put the repair and replacement numbers side by side, check the heat exchanger, and you decide.

items.question: How fast can you come when there's no heat?
items.answer: We answer 24/7, and a no-heat call goes to the front of the line for a same-day visit.
